Oil and gas NDT training in Williston: the short answer

Oil and gas NDT training for Williston is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III instruction in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, delivered live online or onsite at your Bakken facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification stays with your employer's written practice. Atlantis has no classroom in Williston; theory runs online, practicals run on your own specimens and equipment, and cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

The rest of this section is written for two readers. The first is the operations or QA manager at a Williston-area contractor, gathering company or midstream operator who needs technicians certified before the next construction season or facility shutdown. The second is the technician already working in the basin, often as a helper, roustabout or welder's hand, who wants to move into inspection and needs to know exactly what the route looks like. Both need the same thing: a clear picture of which methods the Bakken actually uses, which scheme governs the paperwork, and how to get training done without losing weeks of chargeable field time to travel.

Oil and gas NDT work in Williston and the Bakken

Williston sits in Williams County at the heart of the Bakken and Three Forks play, and almost all NDT demand here is driven by the infrastructure that gathers, processes and moves what the wells produce. That gives the market a different shape from a Gulf Coast refining town. The work is spread across hundreds of square miles, it is weather-bound, and much of it is construction and integrity work on pipe rather than turnaround work inside a single fenced complex.

  • Gas processing. Plants such as Hess Midstream's Tioga gas plant in Williams County and the processing plants operated by ONEOK and others across the basin run pressure vessels, heat exchangers, compressors and large-bore process piping. Their inspection programmes call for UT thickness surveys, weld examination on repairs and tie-ins, and exchanger tube testing during planned outages.
  • Gathering and NGL pipelines. Gas gathering, crude gathering and natural gas liquids lines connect well pads to plants and to long-haul systems. New construction and reroutes generate girth-weld examination to API 1104, and integrity programmes generate dig verification work: UT wall loss, MT for cracking, and visual assessment of coating and corrosion.
  • Long-haul crude and rail terminals. Crude leaves the basin by pipelines such as Dakota Access and by rail loading terminals. Terminal tankage, transfer piping and loading infrastructure carry their own inspection programmes.
  • Well-site and production facilities. Tank batteries, separators, heater-treaters and produced-water handling equipment are pressure-retaining and corrosion-prone. Produced water in the Bakken is a high-chloride brine, and sour service is present in parts of the basin, so corrosion monitoring and crack detection matter.
  • Regional refining. North Dakota's refining footprint sits to the south and east, at the Marathon refinery in Mandan and the renewable diesel plant in Dickinson, and both draw on contractors who also work the basin. The Atlantis Dickinson refining NDT consulting page covers that side of the state.

Three things set Williston apart for training. The first is seasonality: construction and dig programmes concentrate in the warmer months, and winter field work is hard on both people and procedures, so employers try to certify people during the slower period. The second is distance. Sending a crew to a classroom in another state takes them out of the basin for one to two weeks, plus travel, which is exactly why online theory and onsite practicals make sense here. The third is turnover. The basin's workforce has expanded and contracted with drilling activity, and contractors regularly need to bring new hires to Level I and Level II quickly and with paperwork that survives an operator audit.

Which NDT methods Williston oil and gas employers use

The table maps each method Atlantis trains to its Bakken application and the code or standard that usually governs the work. The code is context: your procedure and the operator's specification decide the acceptance criteria, not the training course.

MethodOil and gas application around WillistonCode or standard usually in play
UT (thickness and shear wave)Wall-loss surveys on gathering lines, vessels and tanks; weld examination on repairs and tie-ins at plantsASME Section V Article 4 and 5; operator specifications; API 1104 for pipeline welds where UT is allowed
PAUTGirth-weld examination where the operator accepts it in place of RT; corrosion mapping at dig sites and plant pipingAPI 1104 (mechanised UT provisions); ASME Section V; operator procedures
TOFDThick-wall weld examination at processing plants and vessel repairs; usually paired with PAUTASME Section V; ASME Section VIII code cases where accepted
RTGirth welds on new gathering and transmission construction; plant piping welds to ASME B31.3API 1104; ASME B31.3; ASME Section V Article 2
MTCrack detection at dig sites, compressor station welds and in sour or cyclic serviceASME Section V Article 7; ASTM E709 as reference
PTStainless and non-magnetic components, valve bodies, small-bore fittingsASME Section V Article 6
VTWeld fit-up and final visual on pipeline spreads, coating and external corrosion assessment, plant walkdownsAPI 1104; ASME B31.3; ASME Section V Article 9
ETHeat exchanger and condenser tube testing at gas plants during outagesASME Section V Article 8; plant procedures

Method spotlight for the Bakken: UT and PAUT on pipe. If a Williston contractor trains only one advanced method, it is usually ultrasonic. Thickness work is the volume job on gathering systems and production equipment, and phased array is increasingly what operators specify for corrosion mapping and for girth welds where they want to avoid radiation exclusion zones on a busy right-of-way. A technician who holds UT Level II and is working towards PAUT is the most deployable person on most Bakken crews. See the ultrasonic testing training page for the method itself and the pipeline NDT training page for the pipe-specific detail.

Cold-weather procedure work. Winter in Williston is not a footnote. Penetrant and magnetic particle examinations performed outside the standard temperature range in ASME Section V need a procedure qualified for those conditions, ultrasonic couplant behaves differently in deep cold, and battery-powered instruments lose run time. Atlantis covers these limits in the method courses so that technicians know when to stop and ask for a qualified procedure, rather than finding out from an auditor.

Which certification scheme Williston oil and gas employers expect

Most oil and gas employers in the basin certify their NDT personnel to ASNT SNT-TC-1A through a written practice. Other schemes and credentials appear on job postings, and it helps to know where each one fits. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only; the other schemes are listed here so you can see what local employers also ask for, not because Atlantis offers them.

Scheme or credentialWho asks for it around WillistonDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1A (employer written practice)Most NDT contractors, inspection companies and many operatorsYes. This is what Atlantis trains to
ANSI/ASNT CP-189Some operators and nuclear-heritage clients; less common in the basinPartly. The technical content overlaps, but CP-189 has its own requirements your written practice must meet
Pipeline operator qualification (OQ) under 49 CFR 192 and 195Gas and hazardous liquid pipeline operators for covered tasksNo. OQ is a separate federal requirement administered by the operator or an OQ provider; NDT certification does not replace it
API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certificationOwner-user inspection programmes at plants, terminals and tank farmsNo. These are inspector certifications, not NDT technician certifications. Atlantis does not train for them
AWS CWIConstruction QA on pipeline spreads and fabricationNo. Welding inspection is a separate credential; Atlantis does not train for it
ASNT central (third-party) certification or ISO 9712Occasional international or third-party requirementsNo. Different schemes with their own exams

The practical message for a Williston hiring manager: if your client asks for SNT-TC-1A Level II technicians, your written practice, training records, experience logs and exam records are what an auditor will inspect. Training is one input. The SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains how the pieces fit.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path for Williston technicians, step by step

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It states the methods, levels, training hours, experience hours, exam rules and vision requirements the company uses, and it is signed off by a responsible Level III. No written practice means no certification, however much training someone has.
  2. Classroom training in the method and level. Formal hours in theory, technique and the applicable codes. This is the part that can run live online for Williston crews, so technicians do not have to leave the basin.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented hours performing the method under qualified supervision. Your written practice sets the minimums; the training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. Administered under a Level III. The general exam covers the method principles, the specific exam covers your procedures, codes and equipment, and the practical exam is performed on real specimens. The practical cannot be done online.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually under most written practices.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies the technician against its written practice. The certificate belongs to that employer's programme.
  7. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, with evidence of continuing work in the method. A technician who changes employers in the basin is re-certified under the new employer's practice, though prior training and experience records usually count.

For the Level II detail, including what a Level II may sign and what they may not, see the Level II training path.

Radiography licensing in North Dakota and site access

North Dakota is an NRC Agreement State and has been since 1969, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the state rather than the NRC. The Radiation Control Program sits within the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality. Out-of-state radiography companies coming into the basin for a construction season need a reciprocity arrangement with the state before they work, and North Dakota publishes a reciprocity request form for that purpose. X-ray equipment is also regulated by the state.

For individuals, the radiography rules follow the NRC model: anyone acting as a radiographer must hold a recognised radiation safety certification, work with a second qualified person present at temporary job sites, wear the required dosimetry and alarm ratemeter, and follow the licensee's operating and emergency procedures. Radiation safety training and the radiographer certification exam are separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. A technician needs both to shoot gamma on a Bakken right-of-way: the radiation safety credential to handle the source legally, and the RT certification to interpret film or digital images. Atlantis teaches RT technique and interpretation under SNT-TC-1A; confirm the current radiation safety requirements directly with the North Dakota Radiation Control Program and your company's radiation safety officer.

Site access is the other gate. Operators and midstream companies typically require safety orientation, H2S awareness where sour service is possible, drug and alcohol programme enrolment for pipeline work under DOT rules, and in some cases the operator qualification records described above. None of these are NDT certifications, but missing any of them keeps a certified technician off the site.

Online, live-virtual or onsite: how training reaches Williston

Atlantis does not run a training centre in Williston or anywhere else in North Dakota, and does not pretend to. Training reaches the basin in three ways.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions that technicians join from a man camp, a yard office or home. The formal classroom hours for each method and level can be delivered this way, scheduled around shifts and rotations. See online NDT training for how live sessions and records work.
  • Onsite practicals at your facility. A Level III runs practical sessions at your yard or shop in the Williston area using your instruments, your calibration blocks and specimens that reflect your work: pipe sections with known flaws, corroded plate, weld coupons. Training on your own equipment is the fastest route to a technician who is productive on Monday.
  • Blended cohorts. Theory online over several weeks, then a concentrated onsite block for practical training and exams. For basin contractors this usually means scheduling theory in the quieter winter months and practicals before the construction season starts.

Employer cohorts are the normal model. Individuals can join a cohort, but they still need an employer's written practice to become certified, so an individual technician's first move is usually to secure a sponsoring employer. The corporate NDT training page describes how cohorts are scoped.

Level III services and written practices for Williston NDT companies

Smaller Bakken contractors often grow faster than their quality system. A company that started with two UT thickness technicians and now fields ten people across PAUT, MT and RT may still be running on a written practice written for the original scope, or borrowing one from a previous employer. That is the most common finding in operator audits, and it is fixable.

  • Written practice development and review. Atlantis writes or rewrites SNT-TC-1A written practices that reflect the methods you actually perform. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. Exam administration, procedure review and approval, and personnel qualification for companies without a full-time Level III. Atlantis's Williston refining and oil and gas NDT consulting page covers the consulting side in detail.
  • Procedure writing. Method procedures tied to the codes your clients specify: API 1104, ASME Section V and B31.3, plus cold-weather variants where needed.
  • Audit preparation. A record review before an operator's contractor audit: certifications, vision records, experience logs and exam files.

Book a Level III consultation for your Williston company.

Practise before the practical exam

Atlantis's Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 3D environments, including an oil and gas site and a storage tank, from a laptop. For Williston crews, that means a trainee can rehearse scan patterns, set-up sequences and indication recognition during downtime between hitches. It is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training on real specimens, and it is not a substitute for the practical exam your Level III administers. The Practical NDT page for Williston explains how employers use it alongside onsite sessions, and the UT Level 2 practice questions are a useful check before the written exams.

Your instructor

Training and Level III oversight are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Course content, written practice work and exam administration for Williston cohorts run under his oversight, with sessions delivered online and at the employer's facility.

Frequently asked questions about oil and gas NDT training in Williston

How do I get NDT certified in Williston, North Dakota?

Get hired by, or sponsored by, an employer that certifies NDT personnel to a written practice. Complete classroom training in the method and level, log the required on-the-job experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Training alone does not make you certified under SNT-TC-1A.

Is there oil and gas NDT training in Williston I can do without leaving the basin?

Yes, for the theory. Atlantis runs live online classroom sessions that technicians attend from wherever they are working, and practicals can be run onsite at an employer's Williston-area facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in Williston.

Can I take NDT training online in North Dakota?

Theory hours, yes, if your employer's written practice accepts them, and most do. The practical training and the practical exam must be done hands-on with real equipment and specimens.

Which NDT method is most in demand in the Bakken?

Ultrasonic testing, both thickness and shear wave, is the volume method on gathering systems and production equipment. Phased array is growing for corrosion mapping and girth welds. RT remains important on new pipeline construction, and MT is needed for crack detection at digs and in sour service.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends a minimum number of classroom hours and experience hours for Level I and Level II, and your employer may require more. The training requirements matrix lists the recommended figures. Experience hours usually take longer to accumulate than classroom hours.

Do I need a license to do radiography in North Dakota?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality, or an approved reciprocity arrangement if it is licensed elsewhere. The individual radiographer needs a recognised radiation safety certification and must work under the licensee's procedures. RT certification under SNT-TC-1A is separate and is still needed to interpret images.

Does pipeline operator qualification (OQ) count as NDT certification?

No. OQ under 49 CFR 192 and 195 is a separate federal requirement for covered tasks on regulated pipelines. Many Bakken pipeline jobs ask for both OQ and SNT-TC-1A certification.

What does oil and gas NDT training cost in Williston?

Atlantis quotes on request. The main cost drivers are the methods and levels, the number of technicians, whether practicals run onsite at your facility, and whether you also need written practice or Level III services. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training?

Those programmes generally pay only for schools and courses approved by the VA or listed on the state's eligible training provider list. Atlantis does not claim either approval, so the usual route with Atlantis is employer-paid training. If you need GI Bill or WIOA funding, check with an approved school and with Job Service North Dakota first.

Will Bakken operators accept ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification?

Most do; it is the most widely used framework for NDT personnel in US oil and gas. Always check the operator's contractor specification, which may add requirements such as specific procedures, OQ or site-specific qualification.

Do you train API 570 or API 653 inspectors?

No. Atlantis trains NDT technicians to SNT-TC-1A. API inspector certifications are separate credentials with their own exams.

Can you train our crew at our Williston yard?

Yes. Onsite practicals and exams can run at your facility using your equipment and specimens, with theory delivered online before the onsite block. Ask about onsite training for your Williston crew.
